card.title: Exam bank — every board question on dispersion

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Four questions span this unit: prism i-e-A-deviation derivation (2023), why white light splits (2022), dispersive-power derivation (2021), deviation-vs-dispersion distinction (2020). The through-line: deviation bends single rays (even monochromatic), dispersion sorts wavelengths because refractive index depends on colour.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: deviation = i + e - A (A = r1 + r2) · thin prism = (mu - 1)A · angular dispersion = (mu_v - mu_r)A · dispersive power = (mu_v - mu_r)/(mu_y - 1), dimensionless

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: The i-e-A relation needs the two-face geometry (A = r1 + r2) — meaning each refraction obeys Snell at its own face. Dispersive-power derivation assumes a thin prism (small A, paraxial rays) so deviation stays proportional to (mu-1). Pure spectrum needs slit + collimation; overlapping orders muddy it.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Violet deviates most (highest mu), red least. Achromatic doublet (crown convex + flint concave) cancels colour error while keeping deviation. 2020's distinction trap: deviation happens for monochromatic light too; dispersion needs white light plus mu variation.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: NEB 2023 (4): bend at face one gives d1 = i - r1, at face two d2 = e - r2; total d = (i - r1) + (e - r2) = i + e - (r1 + r2) = i + e - A. NEB 2021 (4): thin-prism deviations dv = (mu_v-1)A, dr = (mu_r-1)A; angular spread dv - dr = (mu_v - mu_r)A; divide by mean (mu_y-1)A for dispersive power.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Mark-losers: calling deviation and dispersion the same thing (2020 tested exactly this); applying the thin-prism form to large angles; forgetting that minimum deviation needs symmetric passage. Cauchy mu = A + B/lambda-squared explains but is empirical.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Two derivations rotate: (a) i-e-A-delta relation from face-by-face bending + quadrilateral geometry; (b) dispersive power from thin-prism deviations of extreme colours divided by mean deviation. Minimum-deviation mu formula belongs to the prisms unit — cite it, don't re-derive, unless asked.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: 'Derive relation' with i, e, A, delta in stem means the face-geometry derivation. 'Dispersive power' means thin-prism extreme-colour subtraction. 'Differentiate deviation vs dispersion' means one ray vs white-light sorting, with monochromatic counter-example.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (4): derive i-e-A-deviation relation. NEB 2022 (3): what is dispersion + why seven colours. NEB 2021 (4): dispersive power expression. NEB 2020 (3): deviation vs dispersion.
